core.title: Map every executable interlocking guard path to exactly one train route or classify it as structural residual
core.given: A plan artifact containing an interlocking with executable guard paths and the train routes projected from it
core.when: The plan reaches the CONFIRM phase (whether or not the interlocking was changed)
core.then: Every executable guard path in the interlocking maps to exactly one train route, unless it is explicitly classified as structural residual.
prefer: For each executable guard path, name the single train route that carries it, so the plan already satisfies the CONFIRM check.
When a guard path truly belongs to no route, mark it explicitly as structural residual instead of leaving it unmapped.
avoid: Leaving an executable guard path with no route and no explicit structural-residual classification.
Mapping a guard path that is not explicitly classified as structural residual to several routes.
Classifying routable guard paths as structural residual just to silence the coverage check.
unless: The guard path is explicitly classified as structural residual.
core.why: A guard path with no train route is a control path no train exercises, and one claimed by several routes has ambiguous ownership; exactly-one coverage keeps the train projection faithful to the interlocking.
evidence: The projection-coverage check passes for every interlocking subject at CONFIRM.
On failure, the finding identifies the interlocking, the guard path, the route involved and a coverage status.
Every executable guard path maps to exactly one train route or is explicitly classified as structural residual.
verification: Enforced only at CONFIRM, the sole enforcement point; the finding is confirm-blocking; disposition strict, severity 4.

Scope: every interlocking in the plan artifact, changed or unchanged; only executable guard paths are checked — non-executable interlocking content is out of scope, and plan artifacts with no interlocking subject are not checked.

The check is a projection-coverage check over the train projection: for each executable guard path not explicitly classified as structural residual, zero mapped train routes fails and two or more mapped routes fails; paths explicitly classified as structural residual are exempt from the exactly-one requirement.
A failure finding reports the interlocking, the guard path, the route involved and a coverage status; the exact field names are realization details.
Observing the trigger needs new observers: the harness must supply the current plan phase, and the interlocking validation subjects are identified by a subject observer, not by a file-kind fact.

fires: At CONFIRM, an interlocking (new, edited or unchanged) has an executable guard path with no train route and no explicit structural-residual classification.
At CONFIRM, an executable guard path that is not explicitly classified as structural residual is mapped to two or more train routes.
At CONFIRM, after a train route was removed from the plan, an executable guard path it covered is left unmapped and not classified as structural residual.
doesNotFire: Any phase other than CONFIRM (e.g. while the planner is still drafting guards or routes); the check is enforced only at CONFIRM.
An executable guard path explicitly classified as structural residual.
Every executable guard path in the interlocking maps to exactly one train route.
Plans that contain no interlocking subject.
Non-executable content in an interlocking (not a guard path).

neutralityNotes: This convention is already expressed entirely in plan-methodology terms (plan artifact, interlocking, executable guard path, train route, structural residual, CONFIRM phase), so the core required no weakening or strengthening; the only realization-specific content in bun.json is identifiers of this one rule's validator and finding format (family/template/variant projection_covers_source::planner_train_interlocking_guard_coverage, the failure-evidence field names, and the implementation/term ids held in the sidecar's audit), all classified bunOnly. profileRequirements is empty because bun.json references no path, suffix, artifact kind or idiom: the obligation lives entirely inside the plan artifact, and a realization resolves plan artifacts through the stack profile (e.g. roles.plan_artifact.kinds, roots.plan) without any per-rule profile need. The subject is not identified by a file-kind fact: the core keeps the Bun note's deference that interlocking validation subjects require a new subject observer and that the harness must supply the phase (needs_new_observer). Severity 4 and disposition strict are kept in core:verification as per-rule facts, not profile keys.
